newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen up 10 pct in yr ahead - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen up 10 pct in yr ahead - Salomon.

text.p: The upside potential for the Hong Kong stock market will range between 10 percent and 15 percent in the year ahead, reflecting expected earnings growth, said U.S. brokerage Salomon Brothers.

"Valuation indicators as a whole suggest the Hong Kong market is currently fairly valued, but earnings outlooks are more favourable compared to other Asian markets," said Deep Kapur, Salomon's chief regional strategist in a recent report.
Declining unemployment, rising consumer confidence and an expected revival in the territory's consumption growth will push its economic growth for 1996/97 above that of 1995, Salomon said.

"Against a background of cyclical recovery in the economy and positive revisions in earnings estimates, compound annual earnings growth ranging between 10 percent and 15 percent is achievable over the 1996/98 period," Kapur said.
Banks and telecommunications are Salomon's favoured sectors while conglomerates and property carry a neutral weighting. Salomon is underweight in utilities and other smaller sectors.
A low price to earnings ratio compared to prospective growth, strong earnings revisions and low earnings uncertainty offer "very attractive" valuations for Hong Kong banks, Salomon said.
"This prognosis is robust to a modest tightening in U.S. monetary policy which would likely widen the net interest margin via an increase in the prime rate but not in funding costs," Salomon said.
Dah Sing Financial, First Pacific Bank, Wing Hang Bank and HSBC Holdings are all favoured stocks.
"We also like Hang Seng Bank at index weight for sector exposure," Kapur said.
Salomon said it holds an overweight position in Hongkong Telecom, whose recent cost control measures are likely to become a significant source of upward revisions by analysts.
While it is neutral on property, Salomon said it is overweight on property investors at the expense of developers.

"We believe that current sales volumes and prices can be maintained in the residential market given the apparent reluctance of potential buyers to overstretch themselves," Salomon said. "In contrast, fundamentals for office market demand are improving."

Salomon said it is overweight in Wharf Holdings, Hysan Development and Great Eagle. Even though it is underweight on developers in general, Salomon is overweight on Henderson Land and New World Development because of their exposure to the office rental sector.
The utilities sector is expensive both relative to macroeconomic conditions and the earnings growth outlook, Salomon said. Hongkong & China Gas is the only utilities stock in the firm's portfolio.
